title: Retention deletes resurrected by in-flight discovery scans

required_properties: A discovery scan that began before a KanidmBackup deletion cannot recreate the deleted record
A manifest fetch that answers HTTP 404 with an explicit NoSuchKey code is reported as a distinct permanent outcome in the Job result document, while an ambiguous or denied fetch stays retryable
A record labeled kaniop.rs/discovered=true whose manifest is absent is removed through the normal deletion flow without incrementing kaniop_backup_validation_failures_total
A user-authored KanidmBackup whose manifest is absent is surfaced as a failure with a reason naming the absent manifest and is counted
Deletion of a KanidmBackup always completes within a bounded time even when a discover Job is stuck or its result is unreadable
Records previously parked in Invalid by discovery are cleaned up automatically from a complete repository listing
The grace that bounds the deletion hold covers at least one discover Job lifetime
Regression tests cover the stale-scan race, the manifest classification, and the automatic cleanup
Documentation of conditions, metrics, and alert expectations matches the new behavior
forbidden_changes: Suppress the validation-failure metric for a user-authored backup with an absent manifest
Prune or discard records based on a truncated repository listing
Leave a KanidmBackup Terminating with no bounded timeout
Change retention policy selection or timing to avoid the race
Treat an unreachable or denied manifest as absent
Hand-edit charts/kaniop/crds/crds.yaml or files under examples/
